title: Diagnose malformed application runtime configuration without unnecessary rollback
trigger: A customer-facing application path returns HTTP 500 or another application error after a configuration change while general service readiness and core dependencies may remain healthy.
preconditions: capture the affected route, customer scope, release version, HTTP status, and X-Request-ID
confirm whether the failure began after a configuration or environment change
record the effective runtime configuration source without exposing secrets
compare release/image identity with the most recent healthy baseline
check readiness and core dependency health before changing components
diagnostic_steps: reproduce the customer failure and compare it with a known-good path on the same release when available
correlate the X-Request-ID through Nginx and API logs
look for configuration_error, parsing, validation, or unsupported-value evidence
inspect the effective runtime value for the suspected non-secret configuration key
compare API image ID and release identity to determine whether code changed
confirm PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, proxy, and readiness health
confirm Loki and Tempo correlation for the failing request
distinguish malformed runtime configuration from code regression, dependency outage, missing data, and proxy failure
mitigation_steps: do not roll back application code when the same image is proven healthy with valid configuration
do not restart or modify healthy database, cache, queue, or proxy components
restore the affected configuration key to an approved supported value
recreate only the runtime component that must consume the corrected environment or configuration
reload an unchanged proxy only when required to refresh service discovery after container recreation
retain before/after image IDs, effective configuration evidence, request IDs, logs, traces, and change ownership
validation_steps: confirm the corrected runtime value is effective
confirm release and API image identity are unchanged
re-test the exact customer request that previously failed
confirm readiness and core dependency health remain healthy
escalate for preventive configuration validation when unsupported values were able to reach the runtime
escalation_boundary: Escalate to the application/platform configuration owner when evidence proves an unsupported runtime value, schema mismatch, or deployment-control gap. Escalate to application development when code changes are required to validate configuration safely or improve failure behavior. Escalate to incident command/platform when the malformed setting affects multiple services, the correct value is uncertain, or recovery requires a broad coordinated change.
